J.- Despite service, neither the petitioner nor his counsel appeared' As a rule, nonappearance of petitioner and/or his counsel after due service would result in dismissal of the petition in default. However, upon cursory examination of the available record, we are of the considered view that the petition should be decided on merits, as it involves a short question ofl law, which has been conclusively settlecl by the Supreme Court.

2. IJefore adverting to the legal question involved, we deem it appropriate to mention briefly the facts giving rise to this petition. It is averred that the father of the petitioner had been selving as a Chowkidar in the respondent-department and retired flrom sei:vicc on 0l .10.2006. On this basis, the petitioner seeks issuance ol an zrppropriate writ under Article 199 ol'the Constitution, directing thc respondent-depat-tment to aopoint A.
him against a1y vacant post, according per his qualification, under the quota reserved for children of retired employees.

3. Arguments of learned A.A.G. appearing on behalf of the respondent-department heard. Record perused' 4. on the one hand, the policy governing the retired son's quota, as lbrmulated and circulated vide S&GAD's letter No.SOR-I (S&GAD)4-1I80(Vo1-IID dated 23.05.2000, clearly provides that the quota is exclusively reserved for the children of civil selants retiring on superannuation or invalidation' Notably, the petitioner's father did not retire upon attaining the age of superannuation, nor on account of invalidation, but voluntarily retired from service betbre reaching the age of superannuation. On this ground alone, the petitioner's case does not merit consideration.

5. on the other hand, in the case of Gcneral Post Office Islamabad and others v, Muhammad Jalal (PLD 2024 SC 1276), the Supreme Court has declared as discriminatory and ultra vires to Articles 3, 4, 5(2), 18, 25(l), and 27 of the Constitution, all the rules, policies, memorandums, etc., which provide for the appointment, without open advertisement, competition, and merit, of children and/or family members of employees who retire or die during service.
6. Furthermore, the Supreme Court in Government of a \J Peshawar and others v. Tahir Mushtaq and others (2025 PLC (C.S.) 34) also held as follows:

5. The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan prohibits discrimination as stated in Article 25 and further stipulates and entrenches the principle in rcspect of service of Pakistan in Article 27. In preferring the children of a government servant or reserving seats for them offends the Constitution. The same also detracts from a merit based system of employment. The taxpayers hard earned monies pay for the salaries, benefits and pensions of government servants. The people's interest lies in having the best person for the job, and not to suffer those who secure employment on the basis of a filial relationship. The stated instructions undermine transparency and good governance, therefore, the Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will be well advised to withdraw all such instructions/notifications.

7. As ruled in Allied Bank Limited v. Habib-ur-Rehman and others (2023 SCMR 1232), where the Supreme Court deliberately and with the intention of settling the law pronounces upon a question, such pronouncement is the law declared by the Supreme Court within the meaning of Article 189 of the Constitution and is binding on all Courts in Pakistan.
8. For these reasons, we do not f,rnd any substance in this writ petition. It is, therefore, dismissed.
